summary: Prose unit 1:7-1:12 (the end of the author's introduction, his signature, and the publisher's introduction). Largely faithful, but 1:7 misreads אל דמי לכם (Isa 62:6, "do not be silent") as "should not think it right", leaves Rabbi Shimon's saying unquoted and a sentence in lower case, and 1:11 omits "Talmud" and does not use the fixed forms for רבינו בחיי and סמ"ג. Job 37:18 and Gen 43:14 in 1:12 were not recognised. Two open questions: כלא חד (1:7) and אגרון (1:12). Abbreviation notes in 1:9 and 1:10 are expanded.

patches.value: All the more so, a fortiori, regarding our God, blessed be He, and blessed be His name, that the Torah insisted that one should not attach to Him or associate with Him anything of all created things, whether corporeal or spiritual, as it is said: "He who sacrifices to the gods shall be destroyed, save to the LORD alone." And Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai the Tanna, peace be upon him, said: "Whoever associates the name of Heaven with something else is uprooted from the world." And we should not say that He is one as the others are one, since the Torah has made clear plainly in many places that He is one, unique, apart from all the other ones. Thus, you who mention the LORD, do not stay silent about making known His oneness, may He be blessed, to your children and your disciples, as you are commanded.
patches.reason: אל דמי לכם is Isa 62:6 ("you who mention the LORD, do not be silent"; דמי is silence/rest), not "think it right"; the English had made the verse mean the opposite of the exhortation. Rabbi Shimon's saying follows ואמר, an explicit quotation, so it takes double quotation marks (decisions, Marking); the sentence after it began in lower case.

patches.reason: Literal had the duplicated "the-name the-name-of-Heaven" and rendered אל דמי לכם as "let-it-not seem to-you".
אל is the negative of the prohibition (Isa 62:6), not "let it not".
דמי is silence or rest (Isa 62:6-7), not "seem" (דמה, to resemble).

patches.value: אל דמי: "do not be silent", from Isa 62:6, where the watchmen "who mention the LORD" are told not to keep silent or rest. The noun דמי is silence/rest; it is not from דמה "seem".
patches.reason: Learner note for the corrected word.

patches.value: לכם is an ethical dative ("for yourselves"); the English does not render it separately.
patches.reason: Every word accounted for; לכם was left unexplained.

patches.value: מלהודיע: "from making known". After אל דמי the sense is "do not stay silent about making known". The earlier note ("let it not seem right to you to refrain") was wrong.
patches.reason: Note repeated the mistaken reading.

value: כל שכן and וקל וחומר are the two Talmudic forms of the a fortiori argument, and the English names the argument once, at the start.
The שלא clause depends on הקפידה: the Torah insisted that one not attach to God or associate with Him anything created.
Exod 22:19 is quoted with שנאמר, an explicit quotation, so it takes double quotation marks; the verse itself is in the apparatus.
ולא אמרינן כלא חד כיון ש… is the reasoning: since the Torah has made clear that He is one, we may not speak of Him as one of the ones.

הנה כן המזכירים את ה׳ אל דמי לכם takes Isa 62:6 ("you who mention the LORD, do not be silent") and applies it to teaching God's oneness. אל דמי is "do not be silent" (דמי, silence or rest), לכם is an ethical dative, and מלהודיע "from making known" completes it: "do not stay silent about making known His oneness".
patches.reason: The fifth note read אל דמי לכם as "it should not seem to you"; it is the Isaiah verse.

value: Exod 22:19, quoted with שנאמר: זובח לאלהים יחרם בלתי לה׳ לבדו. The author writes לה׳ where the verse has ליהוה; the English gives 'the LORD'.
Isa 62:6, embedded without quotation marks: המזכירים את יהוה אל דמי לכם ("you who mention the LORD, do not be silent"). The author writes ה׳ for יהוה and continues the clause with מלהודיע אחדותו.
patches.reason: A verse the decisions require to be recognised was not.

value.english: and we do not say, "All is one,"
value.note: כלא חד may be the Aramaic formula "all is one", which the author disowns; the English reads it as "as one", which supplies "that He is one as the others are one".

patches.reason: Decisions are silent on כלא חד. Proposed ruling: it is the Kabbalists' כולא חד ("all is one"), and the author says the Torah's "one, unique from all other ones" excludes it. If accepted, the English becomes: And we do not say, "All is one," since the Torah has made clear plainly in many places that He is one, unique, apart from all the other ones. The translator's reading is kept as the main text until the owner rules.

patches.value: The book The Wars of the LORD makes known the way of the truths of His unity, may He be blessed, according to the Torah and its interpreters, our Rabbis of blessed memory, in the Mishnah, in the Talmud, Bavli and Yerushalmi, and the Midrashim of our Rabbis of blessed memory, and in accordance with the view of the Geonim, Rabbi Saadia Gaon, and Rabbeinu Bachya in Chovot ha-Levavot, and Rabbi Yehuda Halevi in his poems, and in the Kuzari, the Rambam, the Semag (Sefer Mitzvot Gadol) and the author of the Ikkarim, of blessed memory, and as is accepted by every Jew. In it is a severe warning not to worship any created thing, in accordance with the tradition of all our prophets and all our sages, the Tannaim, the Amoraim, the Geonim and the early decisors, from the mouth of Moses, Aaron and the elders, not to deviate from them and not to add to them.
patches.reason: (1) בתלמוד was left out ("Talmud"). (2) רבינו בחיי is fixed as "Rabbeinu Bachya" (pilot ruling), not "our Rabbi Bahya". (3) סמ"ג is fixed as "the Semag (Sefer Mitzvot Gadol)". (4) "who received it" is not in the Hebrew: מפי משה ואהרן וזקנים stands as written. (5) ספר has no article or demonstrative; "This book" added one.

value: Gen 27:22, an allusion without quotation marks: 'the voice is the voice of Jacob, but the hands are the hands of Esau'. The author writes אגרון (fist) where the verse has ידים (hands).
Job 37:18, embedded without quotation marks: חזקים כראי מוצק ("strong as a cast mirror"). The author puts כראי מוצק before חזקים.
Gen 43:14, embedded without quotation marks: ואל שדי יתן לכם רחמים ("and may El Shaddai grant you mercy"). The author stops the verse there, without לפני האיש.
patches.reason: Two embedded verses the decisions require to be recognised: Job 37:18 (ראיות … חזקים כראי מוצק) and Gen 43:14 (ואל שדי יתן לכם רחמים), the second a blessing that Jacob gives his sons.

patches.value: באגרונו: the word אגרון is not an attested word for "fist"; it is probably a misprint for אגרופו ("his fist"), the usual image beside "the voice of Jacob" (Gen 27:22). Translated "fist".
patches.reason: The apparatus says the author "writes אגרון (fist)" as if it were a word. Decisions (Readings from the witnesses) require a difference to be recorded. Proposed ruling: translate "fist", and record in apparatus "אגרון, probably for אגרוף; unattested", to be settled when the 1931 scan is collated.
